summary: Repository-controlled files are injected into the model's context as the user's own memory or learned patterns
description:
### Impact
With ruflo hooks installed globally (`~/.claude/settings.json` running the home-level `hook-handler.cjs`), files committed in a cloned repository are promoted into higher-trust model context:

1. **Persistent memory poisoning.** On every Stop, `doSync` (`.claude/helpers/auto-memory-hook.mjs`, around lines 527-575, into `v3/@claude-flow/memory/src/auto-memory-bridge.ts` lines 767-826) reads the repo's committed `.claude-flow/data/auto-memory-store.json`. Entries tagged `learnings` or `insight` above a confidence threshold, which the attacker sets, are appended verbatim to `~/.claude/projects/<key>/memory/*.md` and indexed into `MEMORY.md`. Claude Code then loads them every session as the user's own memory, and they remain after the repo file is removed. There is no origin check, no injection or secret scan, and no length cap.
2. **Per-prompt injection.** A committed `.claude-flow/data/ranked-context.json` with broad `words` matches almost any prompt. Its `summary` (80 characters, newlines kept) is printed under `[INTELLIGENCE] Relevant patterns for this task` (`intelligence.cjs` around lines 828-834, `hook-handler.cjs` around lines 862-868), with no sanitizing and no "untrusted data" label. The mods `route` copy strips control characters but is also unlabelled.

There is no code execution. This is prompt injection that gains authority and persists.

### Fix
- Only sync or show entries this machine wrote, using a local HMAC or origin marker, and ignore git-tracked files.
- Run the text through the learning-loop `scan()`, strip control characters, and cap and flatten it.
- Label the block as project data, the way `guidance/projection.ts` does.

cwes.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Output Used by a Downstream Component
Improper Validation of Generative AI Output

summary: x.ruv.io gateway: client-supplied X-Forwarded-For bypasses every per-IP limit
description:
### Impact
`clientIp` in `plugins/ruflo-x-gateway/src/security.mjs` (line 11) takes the leftmost `X-Forwarded-For` value, which the client controls. That value feeds `rateLimited` (`server.mjs`, about line 515), `seraphinaAllowance` and `github.allowance` (about line 366).

An anonymous caller who rotates the XFF value on every request escapes the 60/min MCP limit, the 10/hour Seraphina limit and the 60/hour GitHub limit per IP. One client can then exhaust the shared Seraphina daily budget and the GitHub hourly budget, and drive unbounded relay fan-out. This is a denial of service against a public service; no data is exposed.

`registration.mjs` (about line 95) already derives the IP correctly, using the rightmost entry minus the trusted proxy hops.

### Fix
Use `registrationIp(req, hops)` for every per-IP limit.

### Patched
Fixed in ruflo-x-gateway 0.9.2 (#4784): every per-IP limit uses the trusted end of the forwarding chain, the same derivation as registration. Deployed to x.ruv.io on 2026-11-05 as revision ruflo-x-gateway-00054-tas. A rotating X-Forwarded-For burst that passed 75/75 on the previous revision is now rate-limited. Self-hosted gateways: upgrade and set RUFLO_PROXY_HOPS (or RUFLO_REGISTRATION_PROXY_HOPS) to the number of trusted proxies in front of the gateway.

summary: Federation BBS: a pinned peer can forge the origin of an envelope
description:
### Impact
In `mergeEnvelopes` (`v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/mcp-tools/agentbbs-federation.ts`, around lines 370-383), the signature is checked against the syncing peer's pinned key, but `env.origin` is never compared with `peer.nodeId`.

A pinned peer can sign envelopes that claim any other node as their origin, and `federation_bbs_watch` shows them that way. This contradicts what the `peer_add` documentation promises. Related: `maxSeq` is computed over envelopes that failed verification, and `hops` is not signed.

### Fix
Reject an envelope when `origin !== peer.nodeId`, or verify it against the pinned key of the claimed origin. Compute `maxSeq` only from merged envelopes, and sign `hops` or ignore it.

summary: ruvocal: SSRF through user-supplied MCP server URLs
description:
### Impact
A ruvocal chat session (anonymous when login is off) can supply its own MCP server URL and headers. `isValidUrl` in `ruflo/src/ruvocal/src/lib/server/urlSafety.ts` (around lines 37-60), used by `textGeneration/mcp/runMcpFlow.ts` and `routes/api/mcp/health/+server.ts`, behaves as follows:
- it explicitly allows `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `host.docker.internal` and any dotless `http://` name such as `mongodb` or `metadata`;
- it checks only IP literals, so an https hostname that resolves to a private address also passes.

The MCP client connects with plain fetch, so the IP pinning in `ssrfSafeAgent` is skipped, and results and errors come back to the caller. One target reachable this way is the mcp-bridge (see the companion advisory).

### Fix
Allow loopback and dotless hosts only for operator-configured `MCP_SERVERS`, and route MCP transports through a dispatcher that pins the resolved IP.

summary: ruvocal mcp-bridge: a web page can drive the bridge on loopback when no token is set (CORS * and DNS rebinding)
description:
### Impact
In `ruflo/src/ruvocal/mcp-bridge/index.js` (around lines 1065-1100), `requireAuth` lets every request through when `MCP_AUTH_TOKEN` is unset, and `MCP_CORS_ORIGIN` defaults to `*`. The preflight is answered with 204 and allows `Content-Type`.

Any web page the operator visits can therefore send JSON-RPC to `127.0.0.1:3001` and read the response. That exposes the default memory, agents, config, github, system and hooks tools. There is no Host check, so DNS rebinding also works.

The Host/Origin refusal added for #4510 and #4517 went into `@claude-flow/mcp` and does not cover this separate express server. The non-loopback bind guard (line 1954) does not help, because the attack comes from the operator's own browser.

### Fix
When no token is set, refuse requests that carry an `Origin` header or a non-loopback `Host`, send no CORS header by default, or generate a token on first run.

cwes.name: Reliance on Reverse DNS Resolution for a Security-Critical Action
Permissive Cross-domain Security Policy with Untrusted Domains

summary: Prototype pollution through "__proto__" ids in the agent, task and terminal stores
description:
### Impact
The agent, task and terminal JSON stores are plain objects from `JSON.parse`. `IDENTIFIER_RE` in `v3/@claude-flow/cli-core/src/mcp-tools/validate-input.ts` accepts `__proto__` and `constructor`, so `store.agents["__proto__"]` resolves to `Object.prototype`. That value is truthy, so the existence check passes and the handler writes onto it.

Affected handlers include `agent_update` and `agent_terminate` (`agent-tools.ts`), `task_complete`, `task_update` and `task_cancel` (`task-tools.ts`), and `terminal_close` (`terminal-tools.ts`). For example, `agent_update {agentId:"__proto__", status:"x", config:{…}}` makes every object in the server process inherit `status` and the caller's `config` for the life of the process. That can be used to tamper with logic or to cause a denial of service. This was reproduced in node.

#4671 fixed only the DAA, workflow and claims stores.

### Fix
Reject `__proto__`, `constructor` and `prototype` in `validateIdentifier`, look records up with `Object.hasOwn`, and build collections with `Object.create(null)` in `readRecordStore` and the terminal, swarm and neural loaders.

cwes.name: Improperly Controlled Modification of Object Prototype Attributes

summary: memory_export writes to an arbitrary path and memory_import reads one
description:
### Impact
**Write.** `memory_export` (`v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/mcp-tools/memory-tools.ts`, around lines 1726 and 1802) calls `writeFileSync(outputPath, …)` with no `validatePath` and no workspace containment. An MCP caller can overwrite any file the user can write. If the caller first stores a value containing shell syntax and exports into a file the shell reads at startup (`~/.bashrc`), the JSON line runs as a command on the user's next shell. `~/.ssh/authorized_keys` and other config files can also be overwritten.

**Read.** `memory_import` (around lines 1844-1846) reads any `inputPath` and echoes the JSON parse error, which includes the first bytes of a non-JSON file such as `/etc/passwd`.

**Database path.** `dbPath` (`resolveDbPathOption`) is resolved without containment in every memory tool.

This is the same class as the `session_export` path traversal fixed in #4671 (d369bb73b); this sibling was missed.

### Fix
Apply the realpath containment helper from the `session_export` fix to `outputPath`, `inputPath` and `dbPath`, refuse symlinks, and return a generic parse error.

External Control of File Name or Path

summary: browser_open passes caller-supplied Chromium launch flags, allowing command execution
description:
### Impact
The `browser_open` MCP tool (`v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/mcp-tools/browser-tools.ts`, the handler around lines 172-179) validates only `url` and `session`. `input.args` is joined with commas and passed to agent-browser as `--args`, which forwards it to the Chromium it launches.

Chromium has launch flags whose values are commands it runs: `--renderer-cmd-prefix`, `--gpu-launcher` and `--browser-subprocess-path`. Passing one of them through `args` makes Chromium run the command as the user. Any MCP caller can do this, including a model that follows a prompt injection. A harmless marker script was confirmed to run in a scratch directory.

The ADR-401 hardening (`execFileSync`, no shell) does not help: these flags are legitimate Chromium arguments.

### Fix
Allow only a short list of launch flags (for example `--disable-gpu`, `--disable-dev-shm-usage`, window size), reject every other flag, reject entries containing commas, and apply the same check to every other place that forwards caller args into `execBrowserCommand`.

### Credit
Found in an internal review on 2026-11-04.

cwes.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command
Improper Neutralization of Argument Delimiters in a Command

summary: Unauthenticated RCE in ruflo MCP bridge default docker-compose deployment
description:
The MCP bridge shipping in ruflo/docker-compose.yml exposed POST /mcp with no authentication. The docker-compose defaults bound the bridge and MongoDB to all interfaces. Combined, an unauthenticated network attacker could invoke tools/call → terminal_execute inside the bridge container, obtain a shell as node (uid 1000), read every provider API key from the container env, spawn attacker-controlled swarms on the victim's keys, and persist a poisoned pattern into the AgentDB learning store that steers future AI outputs for all users of the instance.

The tool blocklist that mentions terminal_execute was enforced only in the autopilot flow. POST /mcp and POST /mcp/:group bypassed it.

Fixed in ADR-166 Phase 1-3 (branch security/adr-166-mcp-bridge-rce, PR #2521):
- Bind loopback by default; fail-closed on public-bind opt-in without MCP_AUTH_TOKEN
- Bearer auth middleware (timingSafeEqual constant-time compare)
- Server-side executeTool gate for terminal_execute (MCP_ENABLE_TERMINAL=true opt-in)
- MongoDB --auth on by default; MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_PASSWORD required to boot
- read_only container + tmpfs
- CORS allowlist wiring
- CI regression locks (static + runtime + compose defaults)

Operators of any exposed instance MUST:
1. Firewall :3001 and :27017 immediately
2. Rotate OPENAI / GOOGLE / OPENROUTER / ANTHROPIC keys
3. Audit the AgentDB pattern store for injected agentdb_pattern-store entries; purge poisoned patterns. A patched redeploy alone does NOT undo poisoning.
4. Audit MongoDB for tampering

Credit: [Eli Ainhorn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/eli-ainhorn), Senior AI Vulnerability Researcher @ [Noma Security](https://noma.security) 

Reviewed by Dragan Spiridonov (ADR-166 co-author).
